Maintaining the 5.25–5.50% target range, keeping interest on reserve balances at 5.4%, and continuing balance-sheet runoff signal a rule-like, systematic stance consistent with the post-Volcker literature—e.g., Taylor-rule/estimated reaction functions in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler—and an inflation-forecast–targeting approach in Svensson & Woodford (2005). By insisting on “greater confidence” that inflation is sustainably heading to 2%, the Committee leans on credibility to limit time-inconsistency–driven inflation bias, anchoring expectations (a core theme in modern New Keynesian frameworks linking inflation to marginal costs/expectations). While this is restrictive for near-term demand, the statement’s “better balance of risks” and moderating job gains suggest improved soft-landing odds, a stability-positive but not yet dovish message.
